newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-SBC hailed top Swiss bank after H1.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-SBC hailed top Swiss bank after H1.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp (SBC), smallest of Switzerland's "Big Three" global banks, emerged as the sector's star performer in the first half following a major internal shake-up last year, analysts said on Wednesday.
SBC, reporting as the last of the three major banks on Wednesday, said net profit jumped 84 percent in the first six months of 1997 to 1.326 billion Swiss francs.
Profit growth in percentage terms was accentuated at all three banks by the huge extraordinary provisions taken last year in settling a backlog of bad Swiss domestic loans.
Moreover, the banks reorganised last year into more focused global divisions to boost profitability and cut costs, especially in the over-banked Swiss domestic market.
But even in a climate of massive profit upswings, SBC's 84 percent profit growth was well above market forecasts of between 50 and 70 percent.
It was also ahead of rivals Credit Suisse Group at 70 percent and Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS ) at 67 percent.
"SBC is clearly the best of the three big banks," said senior analyst Hans Kaufmann at Bank Julius Baer in Zurich.
"Also, gross (operating) profit was significantly stronger than at the two other banks," Kaufmann told Reuters.
SBC's operating profit rose 27 percent to 2.617 billion francs, while UBS's operating profit gained only 8.5 percent and CS Group reported an increase of 23 percent.

Analysts praised SBC's underlying performance, which included a 60 percent rise in net profit at SBC Warburg to 691 million Swiss francs -- the first time investment banking has made the largest profit contribution.
"The quality of the bottom-line is a good deal better (than at the other two banks)," said Paul Casanova at Rued, Blass & Cie, a private bank arm of insurer Zurich Group.

A final comparison of the three banks will have to wait until August 27, when CS Group publishes a detailed breakdown of the provisional half-year figures it provided this week in unveiling surprise takeover plans.
CS Group's offer to buy Swiss insurer Winterthur, creating one of the world's biggest financial services companies, overshadowed news of its six-month performance.
But even without a breakdown of CS Holding, analysts said SBC had come out on top.
SBC trading income was up 43 percent from a year earlier, including a 63 percent boost in income from equities trading.
That compared with an overall rise of just one percent in UBS trading income, caused mainly by a surprise loss in equities trading, which fell 52 percent due to problems with derivatives trade.
"We know that SBC is the most professional in estimating credit risk. They are also very professional traders and risk managers, for example in derivatives," Susanne Borer from Bank Vontobel said.

One potential problem is rising payroll costs. Booming world financial markets meant higher bonuses for successful traders, and a weaker Swiss franc made sterling and dollar salaries in London and New York more expensive.
"It is not alarming but it is something to watch," said Werner Huber from LGT Bank in Liechtenstein.
SBC total expenses rose 29 percent for the first half-year. CS Holding reported a provisional 28 percent hike in expenses, while UBS said costs rose 20 percent.
SBC's half-year results cemented its position as a "buy" recommendation among many brokers, including LGT Bank, Bank Vontobel, Zurich Kantonalbank and Rued, Blass. -- Zurich Newsroom, +41-1-631 7340
